content.Summary: The guideline recommends initiating antihypertensive drug therapy with 2 first-line agents for adults with stage 2 hypertension and an average BP more than 20/10 mm Hg above their target. For adults with stage 1 hypertension and a BP goal <130/80 mm Hg, initiating treatment with a single antihypertensive drug is reasonable. Combination therapy is favorable for higher BP control, especially in those with high CVD risk or a history of hypotension. Recommendations also emphasize tailoring drug therapy to individual traits.
Recommendations: Initiate antihypertensive therapy with 2 first-line agents for patients with stage 2 hypertension.
Single-agent therapy is reasonable for stage 1 hypertension with a BP goal <130/80 mm Hg.
Considerations: Combination therapy is often required for effective BP control.
Caution advised when initiating 2 drugs in older adults due to potential hypotension.
Therapy should be tailored to individual patient characteristics and comorbidities.
